data.title: Stock market jitters sap confidence
data.description:
AI CAUTION: The consumer confidence index fell 0.36 points from a month earlier, with the stock market gauge the only one of the survey’s six subindices to decline

Taiwan’s consumer confidence weakened this month, a survey released yesterday by National Central University (NCU) showed, with experts linking it to concerns over the development of artificial intelligence (AI) fueling global market volatility and making investors increasingly cautious.

The consumer confidence index (CCI) fell 0.36 points from a month earlier to 65.91 in the survey — which was conducted last week from Wednesday to Saturday — marking its second consecutive monthly decline.

The CCI measures consumer sentiment for the subsequent six months across six categories: consumer prices, the domestic economic climate, the stock market, purchases of durable goods, employment prospects and family finances.

However, only the stock market gauge declined in the latest survey, falling 3 points from a month earlier to 32.86.

On Friday last week, the TAIEX, the Taiwan Stock Exchange’s benchmark index, plunged 2,393.60 points, or 6.23 percent, to close at 36,033.29, its lowest level in nearly seven months, amid mounting concerns over AI development exacerbated by the resignation of Jensen Huang (黃仁勳) as Nvidia Corp’s chief executive officer.

Dachrahn Wu (吳大任), director of NCU’s Research Center for Taiwan Economic Development, told reporters that the stock market subindex fell by only 3 points despite the TAIEX’s sharp decline on Friday last week because intervention by the National Financial Stabilization Fund helped it recover some of its earlier losses.

The Financial Supervisory Commission’s decision to further tighten short-selling rules also helped curb the sell-off, Wu said.

On Tuesday, the TAIEX rebounded sharply, surging 3,310.46 points, or 8.99 percent, to close at 40,122.35, its largest single-day points gain, after Huang returned to Nvidia a day earlier.

However, the index gave up more than half of those gains on Wednesday, falling 1,926.92 points, or 4.80 percent, to close at 38,195.43.

Wu attributed the market volatility to persistent concerns over AI financing, saying investors feared a funding shortage in the industry could have cascading effects throughout the sector.

Investors were also concerned that AI development in the US could slow following the midterm elections, in which Democrats, who have expressed reservations about the establishment of AI data centers, scored major victories, he said.

Investors were wary of further US restrictions on semiconductor exports to China amid lingering trade tensions between the world’s two largest economies, he said.

Despite the decline in the overall CCI, the subindices for consumer prices, employment, household finances and the domestic economic climate rose 0.37, 0.19, 0.14 and 0.13 points from a month earlier to 37.91, 77.89, 81.02 and 82.82 respectively.

The subindex for purchases of durable goods was unchanged at 82.97.

Meanwhile, the home-buying index compiled jointly by NCU and Taiwan Realty Co (台灣房屋) was unchanged at 90.64 in the latest survey.

This month’s CCI survey garnered 3,259 valid responses from people in Taiwan aged 20 or older. It had a confidence level of 95 percent and a margin of error of 2.0 percentage points.

data.title: CASwell targets revenue growth
data.description:
DOUBLE DIGITS: The firm this month signed a five-year contract with a US firm worth about NT$900 million, with other US projects in the proof-of-concept stage

Industrial computer maker CASwell Inc (瑞祺電通) yesterday said it is targeting double-digit percentage revenue growth next year, supported by a large order from a major US cloud service provider for industrial computer hardware design and manufacturing, as well as global distribution and service support.

CASwell is a subsidiary of Ennoconn Corp (樺漢科技), which has a 27.27 percent direct stake. Ennoconn is an industrial computer arm of Hon Hai Precision Industry Co (鴻海精密).

“Based on our current technology, product portfolio and market development, we are very optimistic about our growth momentum,” CASwell chairman Steve Chu (朱復銓) told an earnings conference in Taipei.

CASwell expects revenue from the US customer to more than double next year from this year’s NT$500 million to NT$600 million (US$15,18 million to US$18.21 million), as it is expanding hardware and services business globally, company president Reaforl Hung (洪德富) said.

Earlier this month, CASwell signed a new five-year contract worth about NT$900 million, making CASwell the sole provider of hardware and global services, Hung said.

The customer is expected to deliver higher gross margin at about 30 percent than the corporate level, the company said.

Other US projects remain in the proof-of-concept stage, Hung said.

In addition, its partnership with Network Box is expected to deliver revenue growth, with CASwell holding a 70 percent stake in the Hong Kong-based cybersecurity provider, he said.

CASwell expects the deal to contribute about NT$200 million in annual revenue through supplying hardware appliances to run cybersecurity software, he said.

Addressing supply chain constraints, CASwell said it is relatively optimistic about DRAM chip supply and pricing, in expectation of an increase in supply by the end of this year, Hung said.

However, PCB supply is more a concern for CASwell, given long lead times, he said.

To address tight supply, the company is diversifying suppliers and certifying second sources, he said.

CASwell reported 28 percent sequential growth in revenue for last quarter to NT$1.71 billion, representing annual growth of 76.6 percent.

Net profit surged 61.6 percent quarter-on-quarter to NT$186 million last quarter. On an annual basis, net profit soared 136.3 percent.

Earnings per share rose to NT$2.5 last quarter, up from NT$1.55 the previous quarter and NT$1.06 a year earlier.

Gross margin improved to 24.4 percent last quarter from 24.2 percent in the second quarter and 22.7 percent a year earlier, supported by domain and cloud-related products for the US-based cloud service provider customer, CASwell said.

data.title: Machinery firms see limited tariff hit
data.description:
Proposed US tariffs of up to 15 percent on Taiwanese goods are expected to have a limited effect on the machinery industry, as the levies would put Taiwanese machinery makers on an equal footing with their major competitors in Japan and South Korea, industry executives said.

The Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) on Wednesday said it had determined that policies and practices related to manufacturing overcapacity in 14 economies, including Taiwan, burdened or restricted US commerce, paving the way for possible tariffs under Section 301 of the US Trade Act.

In July, the USTR announced tariffs of 10 or 12.5 percent under a separate Section 301 investigation into forced labor practices involving goods from 60 trading partners, with some Taiwanese goods facing a 10 percent levy.

The tariffs resulting from the two investigations are expected to result in a tariff rate of 15 percent on Taiwanese goods, rather than being imposed in addition to existing most-favored-nation duties or the proposed 10 percent tariff under the forced labor investigation.

The measures proposed this week have yet to take effect.

Written comments are due on Jan. 5, with public hearings scheduled to begin on Jan. 25, the USTR said.

Yang Te-hua (楊德華), chairman of machine tool maker Goodway Machine Group (程泰機械集團), told reporters that the 10 percent tariff from July was lower than the 12.5 percent rate for Japan and South Korea.

However, the 15 percent rate proposed on Wednesday would put Taiwan on an equal footing with the two countries, meaning the latest proposal is unlikely to erode Taiwan’s competitiveness in the US market, Yang said.

Turning to competition from China, Yang said that effective US tariffs on Chinese-made goods could rise to 24 to 25 percent from 19.9 percent in September.

Such an increase would benefit Taiwanese exporters competing with their Chinese counterparts in the US market, although Chinese manufacturers tend to compete on price to gain market share, he said.

Lin Sung-yi (林松益), chairman of Sun Firm Machinery Industrial Co (三鋒機器), said that Taiwan’s industrial sector had become “somewhat immune” to frequent changes in US tariff policy, as manufacturers have diversified into markets beyond the US.

As long as tariff rates remained “within a fair range,” machinery and machine tool makers were confident they could compete, Lin said.

Yang urged Taiwanese manufacturers to closely monitor the New Taiwan dollar’s performance, saying that currency movements could affect their global competitiveness.

data.title: Singapore says it is ‘engaging’ with firms on exports
data.description:
Singapore yesterday said that it was “engaging” with local businesses over tightened US export controls on Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, but said it could not confirm reports that the firm had halted server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries.

Citing national security concerns, the US has since 2022 restricted exports to China of Nvidia’s industry-leading chips, which are used to train and run AI tools.

Washington last week moved to close a loophole in those controls in the wake of a scandal that forced out chief executive officer Jensen Huang (黃仁勳) before his reinstatement on Sunday.

The new US rules crack down on alleged chip smuggling to China, as well as the large gray market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centers in third countries, often in Southeast Asia.

“We are in the process of engaging our businesses, to reach out to them to see how this impacts their businesses,” Singaporean Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong (顏金勇) told a local summit in Singapore.

“I think that our businesses are also organizing themselves to work with different partners to continue to have access,” Gan said.

Singapore would continue to work with the US to give local companies access to high-end chips, he said.

“Many of the operators, hyperscalers in Singapore, are also Americans, and many companies are operating here,” he said. “It’s important for America to also continue to support our services and customers in this region.”

The Financial Times and other media firms cited sources on Thursday as saying that Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers containing its chips to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.

It was unclear how long the halt would last, the reports said, but it could be a temporary measure while data center operators seek clarity on how to obtain a newly required licence.

The scandal surrounding the company erupted following reports of Huang’s affair with Alice Huang — a former executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company under investigation for the alleged transfer of Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of US rules.

Alice Huang, no relation to Jensen, is also reportedly suspected by some US officials of spying for Beijing.

Massive investments from US and Chinese tech giants have driven a data center construction boom in Southeast Asia.

Analysts at Fitch Ratings warned that data center investment across the Asia-Pacific region would “slow and become more selective under tighter US controls over advanced AI chips” and access to computing power.

“Southeast Asian governments will face a more difficult balancing act between retaining access to advanced US technology and attracting investment from Chinese technology companies,” the Fitch analysts said in a note published on Thursday.

data.title: Sources say SAP mulling cuts of at least 10,000 roles
data.description:
SAP SE is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions to transform its software business for the artificial intelligence (AI) era, people familiar with the matter said, following reductions at Oracle Corp and Microsoft Corp.

SAP’s restructuring would affect at least 9 percent of the global workforce, the people said, asking not to be identified because discussions are ongoing.

The total number of job cuts has not been finalized and might still change after labor negotiations, they said.

The plans come after SAP, Europe’s most valuable software company, reorganized its executive board twice this year as part of a push by chief executive officer Christian Klein to promote an AI-first strategy.

Two of six board members are to leave the Walldorf, Germany-based company in March.

“SAP continuously reviews its organization to ensure it remains aligned with its strategy and customer needs,” the company said in a statement, declining to comment on whether any job cuts are planned.

As part of the changes, SAP’s leadership will continue to redesign how it develops and sells products, the people said.

Klein is seeking to embed AI tools into the company’s applications after earlier attempts to introduce AI products faced problems.

All departments are being asked to identify areas for potential cuts, with product and engineering and sales departments in particular focus, the people said.

SAP briefly reigned as Europe’s most valuable company last year thanks to strong sales growth as it pivoted from traditional on-premises software licenses to cloud subscriptions. It has shed more than one-quarter of its value since its peak, in part due to investor concerns that AI could allow customers to replace some traditional enterprise software.

The overhaul would add SAP to the list of large software firms shrinking their workforces as they retool their businesses around AI.

Oracle cut 21,000 jobs in 12 months, saying some roles had been eliminated by AI.

Microsoft is offering buyouts to about 60,000 workers.

SAP’s Klein took over most of the responsibilities of product lead Muhammad Alam this year after he did not renew his contract, which ends in March.

Sales chief Thomas Saueressig, who had been given an expanded role earlier this year, last week said that he will leave the company to become CEO of Ionos Group SE.

SAP historically has announced major restructurings in late January alongside its full-year results, most recently in 2024. About 10,000 positions were eliminated in that effort, which cost about 3 billion euros (US$3.3 billion) and took more than a year.

It was mainly handled through voluntary departures and retraining workers, with the total number of employees remaining relatively flat as SAP hired for new positions.

data.title: WinWay capacity ramp-up continues
data.description:
ROSY PROSPECTS: AI adoption is an irreversible trend and key clients are projecting aggressive demand heading into next year, the chip testing interface supplier said

WinWay Technology Co (穎崴) yesterday said it is ramping up capacity through next year to meet surging demand, brushing aside concerns over an artificial intelligence (AI) bubble and US chip export curbs.

The Nvidia Corp leadership upheaval surrounding CEO Jensen Huang (黃仁勳) is not expected to derail AI’s progress, the Kaohsiung-based supplier of integrated circuit testing interface and coaxial sockets said.

“AI adoption is widely recognized across industries as an irreversible trend,” WinWay chairman Mark Wang (王嘉煌) said on the sidelines of a media gathering in Taipei.

“Overall, demand for semiconductor testing interfaces remains robust, despite market uncertainty,” Wang said.“Our key customers, particularly AI suppliers, are projecting aggressive demand heading into next year.”

WinWay is accelerating its in-house probe expansion in Taiwan, aiming to ramp up monthly capacity from 9 million units at the end of this year to 24 million by the end of next year in preparation for customers’ next-generation chips slated for 2028 through 2030, Wang said.

The company’s probe products are key components used in coaxial sockets and load boards for wafer and chip testing. High-end coaxial socket capacity is projected to surge 82 percent year-on-year to 38,200 units this year, it said.

WinWay reported that third-quarter revenue surged to NT$4.56 billion (US$138.4 million) from NT$3.52 billion in the previous quarter and NT$1.8 billion in the same period last year.

The company attributed the robust growth to rising demand for advanced process nodes such as 7-nanometer process technology.

About 73 percent of its revenue came from high-end coaxial sockets and vertical probe cards used to test AI and high-performance computing chips, the company said.

With the capacity expansions, WinWay expects revenue to grow by a double-digit percentage next year, Wang said, adding that this year’s sales growth has been capped by capacity constraints.

To keep pace with customer demand, the company plans to establish new offices in Dallas, Texas, and in Phoenix, Arizona next year, he said.

The company’s US expansion aligns with capacity buildouts by key customers, including Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (台積電), King Yuan Electronics Co (京元電子), Amkor Technology Inc, Texas Instruments Inc and Tesla Inc.

WinWay’s net profit in the third quarter surged about 54 percent sequentially to a record-high NT$1.034 billion from NT$672 million. That represented annual growth of 178 percent from NT$372 million.

Earnings per share rose to NT$28.55 from NT$18.7 in the second quarter and NT$10.38 in the third quarter last year.

data.title: Hua Nan upbeat on profit growth
data.description:
OPERATIONS: The financial holding firm is focused on expanding its core banking business, developing non-banking services and boosting cross-selling

Hua Nan Financial Holding Co (華南金控) yesterday said it expects profits to continue growing next year, supported by sustained investment in artificial intelligence (AI), steady loan growth and expanding wealth management and overseas businesses.

The group remains optimistic about Taiwan’s economic prospects, as investment in AI and technology is expected to remain strong, although global trade policies, geopolitical tensions and financial market volatility could create uncertainties, Hua Nan Financial president Hsiao Yu-mei (蕭玉美) told an online earnings conference.

The company would focus on expanding its core banking business, developing non-bank operations and strengthening cross-selling among subsidiaries to sustain earnings growth, she said.

Interest and fee income would benefit from monetary tightening in the US and Taiwan to curb inflation, Hsiao said.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points next month and possibly again early next year, she said.

Taiwan’s central bank could raise interest rates by 12.5 basis points next month, before keeping them unchanged throughout next year, she added.

The company posted net profit of NT$28.46 billion (US$863.81 million) in the first 10 months, up 26.9 percent from a year earlier and already surpassing its full-year earnings for last year.

Earnings per share reached NT$2.02, a record high.

Hua Nan Commercial Bank Ltd (華南銀行), the group’s main subsidiary, benefited from steady loan growth and an improved deposit and loan mix, lifting net interest income by 12 percent in the first 10 months.

Its wealth management business also gained momentum, with fee income increasing 28.9 percent year-on-year, while revenue from wealth management rose 34 percent.

The number of high-net-worth customers exceeded 3,700, up 83 percent from a year earlier, while assets under management surpassed NT$300 billion, an annual increase of 77 percent, the bank said.

The bank’s offshore banking unit (OBU) and overseas branches generated combined net profit of NT$4.94 billion in the first 10 months, up 39 percent year-on-year and accounting for 21 percent of the bank’s total earnings.

OBU profit surged 124 percent, as the bank sought to capture growing cross-border financial demand arising from global supply chain restructuring, it said.

Hua Nan Securities Co (華南永昌證券) reported net profit of NT$4.36 billion in the first 10 months, up 163 percent year-on-year, benefiting from increased trading activity and higher turnover in the local stock market.

Growth in underwriting, overseas securities trading and digital financial services also contributed to earnings.

The company’s South China Insurance Co (華南產險) posted net profit of NT$1.75 billion, up 24 percent from a year earlier, supported by stronger underwriting performance and investment returns.

Separately, the company said its digital transformation initiatives had generated more than NT$2 billion in benefits, while AI applications at Hua Nan Bank had delivered productivity gains equivalent to more than NT$200 million in labor costs.

data.title: MiTAC expanding capacity to support business growth
data.description:
MiTAC Holdings Corp (神達控股) yesterday said that continued capacity expansion in Taiwan, Vietnam and the US would help the company meet customers’ diverse needs and boost its business growth next year.

“We have continued expanding our global footprint over the past two years, which means we have sufficient capacity and power supply to support our growth, so we are very positive about next year,” MiTAC Holdings president Billy Ho (何繼武) told an investor conference in Taipei.

MiTAC Holdings counts hyperscalers, cloud service providers, neocloud operators and enterprise customers among its customers. The company has a broader rack-system product portfolio for server, networking, artificial intelligence (AI) compute and storage, Ho said.

Customers are increasingly focused on whether suppliers such as MiTAC Holdings have sufficient liquid-cooling capacity and power availability to support future operations, he said.

The company has relatively low revenue exposure to Southeast Asia and China, with its main markets in the US, Europe and other parts of the Asia-Pacific region, Ho said.

AI regulations and political developments in the US following the midterm elections have a limited impact on the company, he added.

MiTAC Holdings continues to expand capacity in Miaoli County’s Jhunan Township (竹南) and New Taipei City’s Linkou District (林口), with a new plant in Taoyuan’s Yangmei District (楊梅) scheduled for completion in 2028, Ho said.

The company is also constructing new facilities in California’s Newark, San Jose and Fremont, after its Vietnamese plant began operations in March, he said.

The company plans to spend US$500 million to US$600 million in capital expenditure over the next two to three years to further expand capacity in Taiwan, Vietnam and the US, MiTAC Holdings chief financial officer Doris Huang (黃秀玲) said.

MiTAC Holdings comprises MiTAC Computing Technology Corp (神雲科技), MiTAC Digital Technology Corp (神達數位) and MiTAC International Corp (神達電腦).

In the first three quarters of this year, MiTAC Computing accounted for 91.6 percent of MiTAC Holdings’ total revenue of NT$118.12 billion (US$3.59 billion), followed by MiTAC Digital Technology at 6.6 percent and MiTAC International at 1.8 percent.

MiTAC Computing’s rack systems for data centers include AI servers, high-performance computing servers, multi-node servers, graphics processing unit-based servers, general-purpose enterprise servers and storage servers, company president Rick Hwang (黃承德) said.

He said the company has increasingly delivered full-rack systems rather than individual servers as customer demand evolves, with rack solutions tailored to customers’ configurations, including those based on Advanced Micro Devices Inc’s (AMD) Instinct and EPYC processors.

The company expects to roll out its liquid-cooled server racks for AMD’s Helios platform next year, he added.

data.title: Eight banks report NT$1.82 million in unauthorized transfers: FSC
data.description:
Eight banks have reported major incidents involving unauthorized online transfers totaling NT$1.82 million (US$55,201) from the accounts of 10 customers, the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) said yesterday.

The eight banks are CTBC Bank Co (中信銀行), E.Sun Commercial Bank Ltd (玉山銀行), Hua Nan Commercial Bank Ltd (華南銀行), Taipei Fubon Commercial Bank Co (台北富邦銀行), Taiwan Cooperative Bank Ltd (合庫銀行), Chang Hwa Commercial Bank Ltd (彰化銀行), First Commercial Bank Ltd (第一銀行) and Taishin International Bank Co (台新銀行), FSC Banking Bureau Secretary-General Chen Chia-chen (陳家珍) said at a news conference.

Separately, the Criminal Investigation Bureau (CIB) said it had received more than 100 reports of unauthorized online banking transfers that occurred between September and Nov. 11. Reported losses totaled NT$17.42 million.

The CIB said 22 financial institutions were affected, including 18 banks, one securities brokerage and three electronic payment providers.

The bureau said it suspected that criminals had used malware hidden in an Android app posing as a short-form video app to take control of users’ phones and transfer money through their mobile banking apps.

Asked about the difference between the two sets of figures, Chen said banks decide whether incidents meet the FSC’s criteria for reporting as major contingencies, while the CIB compiles reports from the public.

In the case involving the securities brokerage, an investor had reported that an order was placed without their knowledge, FSC Securities and Futures Bureau Deputy Director-General Huang Chung-hao (黃仲豪) said.

The brokerage had not reported the incident as a major contingency, but the Taiwan Stock Exchange Corp was looking into it, Huang said. He added that in some cases, investors who suspected their orders had been tampered with later realized they had scheduled the orders themselves.

Asked how customers could seek compensation and whether banks would be held responsible, Chen said the outcome would depend on the circumstances of each case. Customers dissatisfied with the outcome could seek mediation through the Financial Ombudsman Institution, she added.

Chen said the FSC had instructed financial institutions to strengthen their cybersecurity defenses and resilience. In response to the methods described by the CIB, the commission would ask the Bankers Association to discuss ways to improve existing security measures.

The FSC would also work closely with law enforcement agencies and cooperate fully with police investigations, she said.

The commission would ask financial institutions to remind customers to avoid downloading apps from unknown sources or clicking on unfamiliar links, Chen said.
